name: rf-treediff
title: Robinson-Foulds (TreeDiff)

scalars.description: Should equal **half** the built-in `rf` metric exactly. TreeDiff halves the symmetric difference and the built-in metric does not (since v2, §34.19), so `rf == 2 * this`; any other relationship means one of them is wrong. The pattern is anchored to the start of a line on purpose: `rf_postorder` switches to printing "Weighted Robinson Foulds distance is:" when its input carries branch lengths, and an unanchored pattern matches that line too — recording a weighted distance of 1.23e+06 as an RF of 6,825's kind. The server writes this metric's input without lengths, so it does not currently happen; anchoring makes it refuse rather than depend on that staying true.

description: Robinson-Foulds computed by TreeDiff, the reference implementation of Branco, Vaz & Francisco (2024), run as a separate process over a succinct balanced-parentheses representation. Registered as an independent check on the built-in `rf` metric rather than for speed: it is a different algorithm over a different representation by different authors, and three of the five RF implementations examined for this project return wrong answers on real input. `rf_postorder` is chosen over `rf_nextsibling` because it uses an explicit stack; the latter recurses per tree level and these trees are 604 deep.
